newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian textile firm delists from bourse.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian textile firm delists from bourse.

text.p: Nigerian textile firm Westex was on Monday removed from the daily official list of the Nigerian stock exchange, a senior official said.
The company applied to delist from the textile sector of the market last year and asked shareholders to surrender their certificates in exchange for cash payment.
"They have complied with all conditions for delisting up to 98 percent," Aghatise Erediauwa, an official of the exchange who moderated Monday's trading session told dealers.
Erediauwa said the company had paid off most of its shareholders but those left were the few it had not been able to contact.
He said Westex had deposited the amount for the oustanding amount with the exchange's clearing house to safeguard the investors' money.
Analysts said a harsh operating environment forced Westex to diversify into sales and service of Japanese brands of vehicles from its core business of textile manufacturing.
The company did not pay any dividend for the year ended 1995, its last year of reporting to the exchange.
It was incorporated in 1969 as Western Textile Mills and was listed on the bourse on March 27, 1980.
It traded at 5.60 naira on April 3,1996, the day of the last recorded transaction in its shares.
Only six firms remain on the official list of the textile sector on the Lagos bourse with the exit of Westex.
